To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the type of myo-sin expressed by individual muscle fibers is determined by their motor unit type and that the myosin of cross-reinnervat-ed muscle fibers can be converted to that of another motor unit type, but not completely.
the myosin isoforms of skeletal muscle fibers can be altered by cross-reinnervations, and that the extent of the alteration is dependent on the muscle fiber type and on the nature of the innervation.
the myosin of skeletal muscle fibers can be altered by cross-reinnervating the nerve supply to the muscle, and the extent of the transformation depends on the muscle type.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between the contractile proteins, myosin, and the physiological properties of skeletal muscle fibers.
the relationship between the contractile properties of skeletal muscle fibers and their innervation.
the relationship of contractile properties of skeletal muscle to its nerve supply.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the myosins of individual motor units in normal and cross-innervated cat skeletal muscles have been shown to be distinctive and to be under the control of the innervating nerve.
cross-reinnervation results in the synthesis and incorporation of new myosin in the muscle fibers of both slow and fast muscle.
cross-reinnervation does not change the myosin of the FDL, and that it changes the myosin in the SOL only in part.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the myosin of cross-reinnervating muscle fibers can be transformed, apparently to the extent that it is completely replaced, by myosin of the nerve source.
myosin isoforms can change in response to altered nerve activity, but that the myosin isoform present in a given muscle is not necessarily a function of the activity pattern alone.
the myosin of skeletal muscle fibers is under genetic and environmental control.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the myosin isoform composition of a muscle is determined by the activity of the motor units that are innervated by its motor neurons.
the myosin isozyme of a muscle cell is determined by the motor neuron that innervates it.
the myosin isoforms in the skeletal muscle fibers of cat are not only regulated by nerve activity but also by the muscle fiber type.
